steps.title: Key Point
steps.body: You MUST discuss BOTH the extract AND the whole play. Ignoring either will cost you marks.

steps.title: The Bridge Method
steps.body: After analysing the extract, add a paragraph that connects to the wider play. Use phrases like: "This moment echoes..." "Earlier in the play..." "This contrasts with..." "Later, we see..."

steps.title: Extract Analysis Strategy
steps.body: Spend 5 minutes reading and annotating before writing. Identify 3-4 key quotations to analyse in depth. Roughly 2/3 of your essay should analyse the extract; 1/3 should link to the whole play. Use the "Bridge Method": after analysing a quotation, bridge to the wider play with phrases like "This moment echoes..." or "Later, we see..."

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: What should you look for in a close reading of an extract? | How do you embed a quotation effectively? | What's the difference between extract analysis and whole-play linking?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Look for: key quotations rich in language techniques; structural features (verse/prose, soliloquy); effects on audience; connections to themes and whole play. | Embed by integrating the quotation into your sentence structure. Instead of "He says 'quote'. This shows...", write "Macbeth's use of 'quote' reveals..." - make the quotation part of your analysis. | Extract analysis focuses on the specific lines given: word choice, imagery, structure within that passage. Whole-play linking connects to scenes before/after, tracking character development and themes
